literal: point at a deer and call it a horse
meaning_long: deliberately twisting the truth and making others go along with it
source: 《史记·秦始皇本纪》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
story: Ancient China, the Qin dynasty. Zhao Gao is the most powerful minister at court, and he wants to know who dares to disagree with him. He brings a deer to the young emperor and says: 'Your Majesty, here is a fine horse!' The emperor laughs: 'That is a deer!' Zhao Gao turns to the officials. Most of them are scared of him, so they say: 'Yes, it is a horse!' The few honest officials who say 'deer' soon get into big trouble.
continuity: - ZHAO GAO, the minister: tall, thin man about 50, narrow sly eyes, long thin black mustache and a pointed beard, tall black official hat, dark purple robe, a smug smirk.
- THE YOUNG EMPEROR: a teenager with a round, innocent face, golden robe and a flat crown with a beaded fringe, sitting on a big throne.
- THE DEER: a gentle spotted brown deer with small antlers and big, confused eyes, led on a red rope.
- THE COURT: a grand throne hall with red pillars and a polished floor; the officials wear identical slate-blue robes and black hats and are simple background figures.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

In the throne hall: Zhao Gao points at the confused deer on its red rope with a grand, smug gesture, smirking; behind him a row of nervous officials sweat and nod. Zhao Gao's face and the deer's face clear. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
Zhao Gao strides proudly down a palace corridor with his nose in the air while officials on both sides bow deeply and nervously.
Zhao Gao leads the deer by its red rope into the throne hall; the young emperor on the throne leans forward, curious.
Zhao Gao bows with a theatrical flourish, presenting the deer with an open hand and a sly smirk. The deer blinks, confused. (Only Zhao Gao and the deer.)
The young emperor laughs on his throne, pointing at the deer and holding his belly. (Only the emperor, with the deer at the edge of the frame.)
A row of officials, sweating and pale, nod and bow eagerly toward the deer, forcing big fake smiles; Zhao Gao watches them with narrow, satisfied eyes.
One honest official in a slate-blue robe is led out of the hall by two palace guards, looking back sadly; in the background Zhao Gao smirks. No weapons drawn, nobody hurt.
The rope (background for the big title)

The deer's red rope lying loose on the polished hall floor next to a few small hoofprints, in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is a calm, plain hall wall with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing on it (we place the big title there). No people, no animals.

A modern meeting room: the same ZHAO GAO (narrow sly eyes, thin mustache, pointed beard) as a boss in a dark purple suit proudly points at a whiteboard with a clumsy, obviously wrong drawing of a deer (simple lines, no words, no numbers), while three employees nod nervously, sweating, with forced smiles. No text, no logos, no screens.
lines: He pointed at a deer and said: what a fine horse!
This minister was the most powerful man at court.
He brought a deer to the young emperor.
Your Majesty, here is a fine horse!
The emperor laughed: that is a deer!
But the officials were scared, and said: yes, a horse!
The few who said deer got into big trouble.
Point at a deer, call it a horse.
It means twisting the truth, and making others agree.
Like a boss who calls a bad idea brilliant, and everyone nods.
title: He pointed at a deer and called it a horse 🦌 | 指鹿为马
desc: 指鹿为马 (zhǐ lù wéi mǎ) = deliberately twisting the truth and making others go along with it. Ever seen that? 👇
pinned: 指 point · 鹿 deer · 为 as · 马 horse. 📝 他明明错了还要大家同意，真是指鹿为马。(Tā míngmíng cuò le hái yào dàjiā tóngyì, zhēn shì zhǐ lù wéi mǎ.) = He's clearly wrong but makes everyone agree; that's calling a deer a horse.
